page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The instance operates with dedicated CPU allocation, ensuring consistent compute performance without resource sharing or CPU credit limitations.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, making it reliant on network-attached storage options for persistent data. Additionally, the instance does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n4d-highcpu-16 is structured for compute-heavy workloads that require substantial processing power relative to memory capacity. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for tasks such as batch processing, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, web serving, and distributed compute tasks where high memory overhead is unnecessary.
